reports.title: Harvey Pass
reports.text:
27 Nov 26, 11.45am
EL 2190m, N aspect
Overcast
Air -3.9C
HST 20cm, HS 40cm
Wind L, SW
Surface PP 0.5 - 1
20cm SS on MFcr, unreactive
10-15cm DF Facets below MFcr to base
Good, slightly wind effected skiing in Curveball. Didnt touch the bottom :)

reports.title: More Snow than Expected
reports.text:
Thinking it was low tide still three of us walked up to Arnica Lake to climb Unnamed. 
We didn’t anticipate much snow but found it! Waist deep in the gully sitting on firm older snow. 
We experienced two whumps and a large shooting crack that crossed the whole feature. Then we walked back to the car.

reports.title: Scoping Out The Connaught Drainage After The Storm
reports.text: We skinned from the parking lot which has 0-10cm on the ground. It increases dramatically once on the trail to about 40cm deep. We reliably measured 50cm at 1650m. Great travel conditions on the way up with decent coverage of the trail. The Hospital uptrack was in okay shape requiring some minor acrobatics to get over the usual obstacles. HS at TL is highly variable from 50-120cm. The alpine aroun

reports.title: French creek
reports.text: Observed a fairly large avalanche on Mt. Birdwood from the road where it looked like spindrift had been collecting below the face. I then skinned up French creek a little way and found a filled in, WNW facing gully/ couloir which held about 70-80cm in the middle. I continued to boot up the lower couloir before I found a ~5cm layer of faceted snow sitting atop a firm bed surface with about 60-70cm

reports.title: Metal Dome size 1
reports.text:
Very poor visibility while descending from Metal Dome summit, approaching our line, a rope was thrown to find the convexity. 
A .5m cornice was present on the E-SE aspect which collapsed from ski pressure 1m back from edge. After looping around the corniced face and descending we returned to our skin track at the bottom of the first pitch, it had been covered by a size 1 slab below the cornice. 
~

reports.title: Widespread signs of instability at TL and ALP
reports.text:
Skinning up towards Balu Pass our AST 1 crew observed several recent (within the past 12-24hours) natural size 1-2.5 windslabs that had released out of the lower slopes off Cheops N. Bowl. We also had fairly significant whumpfing as we approached the lower slopes below Balu Pass. 
At a re-group in the flats below Balu Pass we watched as a rider came through some cliffs on the steeper slope lookers

reports.title: Metal Dome Ridge
reports.text: Went up towards Metal Dome to check out the snow situation for our first day out. Marginal coverage on the road and through the forest, but snow depth quickly increased by the meadows. Probed 1.5m snow depth at about 1600m. The highest we got was 1770m due to whiteout conditions above treeline. Skied a couple short laps down from there and saw no signs of instability. Just very heavy wet snow.

reports.title: Metal dome

signs: 30 cm or more of new snow in past 24 hours

reports.text:
No signs of recent avalanche activity, obs were limited due to visibility
Probed 180-220 @1800m depending on wind load

reports.title: Balu Pass
reports.text:
Expected minimal snow and that’s what we got. 
- Balu pass skin track is in alright condition and can begin skinning not far after parking lot
- Skin track follows creek side and doesn’t cross the bridge unlike last season. 
- Once out of the trees skin track has decent coverage. 
- Skied out until just after frequent flyer then transitioned. Lots of sharks still hidden away.
- Found 50cm of Snow

reports.title: Finding Patience
reports.text: Went for an exercise skin on the road up Enterprise Creek. 50-60cm HS @ 1700m. Recent storm snow is moist and heavy. temps were just below freezing. Snowed S1 to S2 the whole time we were there . Got a wet loose type sluff to slide on a steep bank above the road and some 1-2 metre shooting cracks while we briefly poked above the road. That said, it is well below threshold. Wasn’t expecting to ski

reports.text:
We went up to metal dome this afternoon. Parked around 1000m in pouring rain, there was little snow on the ground. 
Started skinning right away regardless. 
The snow quantity got better as we went up and was 1.3M at 1500m . Quality however, did not. Classic coastal concrete. It continued to rain at 1500 when we turned back with water creeping into our GoreTex.

reports.title: A long walk with a tiny bit of skiing
reports.text:
Had plans to go ski off of Young’s Peak but the wind at the Asulkan hut was much higher than what was forecasted. Guessing in the 40km/hr range. Was tough to stand after gusts. 
Noticed some wind slabs forming on Lee features and experienced shoots cracks on the last pitch before the cabin. Very typical for the feature. Wasn’t feeling like getting freezing cold and pushed around so turned around t

reports.title: Burstall pass
reports.text:
Travel and Snow Quality
Skinning conditions were good on the way in. Turns on the East aspect off north Burstall Pass were good, but coverage is thin and you would hit a rock about every 4th turn. Bring rock skis only. On the descent, we hiked down the steeper sections of the trail.
Weather
Temperatures ranged from -6°C to -1°C. Winds were steady moderate West, increasing to strong through the day

reports.title: Wedgemount Lake (early season)
reports.text: Great day snowshoeing. Near the lake there was approximately 30-45cm of snow with substantial wind transport leading to very deep sections. Trail itself leading up to it only had 5-10cm. In the wind loaded sections I sank down to past my knee and there appeared to be a slab forming with some cracks developing in sections. Overall not enough snow to fully ski yet due to rocks below lake but above l

reports.title: Sunshine – Boundary Bowl, beside the slope
reports.text:
Weather: Cloudy, flat light.
Snowpack: HS ~35 cm at 2350 m. Very weak, loose snowpack with no real base. Poles hit the ground quickly, and rocks and shrubs are poking through nearby. Buried Surface hoar was present and felt very unstable. No distinct crust or layering was visible in the snow wall.

reports.title: Crowfoot Falls
reports.text: Bailed off of the last pitch of Crowfoot Falls after getting 2 bouts of significant spindrift. There was about 3-4 cm of new snow on the approach slope and large snow slope after the approach ice pitch. When the wind picked up around 11 AM, we noticed wind blowing snow around us. New D1 dry loose occurred on snow slope above approach ice and occurred while we were climbing around 12 PM.

reports.title: Balu pass - skins from the lot, core shots on the way down
reports.text: Decent coverage on the up track besides a few spots directly under tree cover. Snow was falling sporadically and vis was in and out. Probe at the top of Balu pass reading just shy of 70cm. I tested the waters on a steeper section of the face with a stop above some rocks, my sluff from the stop quickly accumulated sending a growing but very slow moving mass of wet loose snow down in front of me. Ap

reports.title: Rummel Ridge
reports.text:
Went for a scouting mission up Rummel Ridge Monday. Very low coverage below tree line (~5cm). Tree line and above had ~30cm of low density snow. 
Evidence of wind loading on Lee NE Aspects. Need more snow….

reports.title: Wedgemount Lake
reports.text: Significant wind loading and wind-slab formation on leeward aspects (west-facing). In places, the top 8cm were consolidated enough to cause cracks from body-weight. Underlying snow is poorly consolidated powdery, sugar snow. Wind slabs were approx 40-50cm at their deepest.

reports.title: Sinatra Falls

signs: critical warming from sun, warm air temperature, or rain

reports.text:
Approach:
Scouted the route from the road the day prior (22nd). The upper mountain and surrounding bowls appeared to be below threshold for avalanches. Left the vehicle at 0700 with an ambient temperature of approximately −5°C. The approach was bone dry.
Climbing Conditions:
The ice was thin and generally poorly protected, with the longest screw placement being 10 cm. Pitons and nuts proved useful

reports.title: Rock Isle Gully
reports.text:
Skied the gully in the north east corner of Rock Isle Lake near Sunshine Village. The run itself was better than expected but still not a lot of snow there; around 45cm at the top was what I measured. The bottom of the gully is very rocky still. If that area gets at least another foot of snow, it will ski pretty well.
On the snow conditions aspect, I found the wind exposed were starting to get som

reports.title: Grizzly ridge
reports.text:
- 20 leaving the car with clr skies and light winds from the E/SE. Was able to skin from the car park through pocaterra cirque. 
Heading up the fan towards grizzly ridge on a N Asp below 2400 average of 20-30cm HS. 5-15 cm of low density snow overlies a 1-2cm breakable crust.
As I got up into the couloir feature conditions were variable. 
Tracks were still semi visable from a recent party but most

reports.title: Pocaterra Ridge
reports.text:
-19 at parking lot. Skin trail was decently covered at start of day, got exposed by afternoon. Few individuals attempting 2 Couloirs. hs 25-30cm of snow by P.Ridge. Wind loaded areas hs 40-45cm. 
Good enough for exercise, lots of rocks covered in skin material, few turns to be had that resulted in no ill faces.
Slog through trees, ice, rocks, dirt present on approach trail by EOD.
One more storm.

reports.title: Lower Grizzly Col
reports.text:
Skin track has good coverage, well set.
HS varies from 20-40cm. Thin coverage, beware of rocks. 
Quick snow pit @ 2400m, W asp, open slope, 15cm of Fist Snow sit on 12cm of Pencil to Knife Crust from last week warming cycle. Then there is 10cm of 2-3mm Facet to the ground. Crust is hard to break. 
No instabilities observed.

reports.title: Snowmobiling Hurley area
reports.text: 5-10cm fresh snow at 1800m overtop surface hoar

reports.title: Burstall pass
reports.text:
Skin track coverage was good for the most part. 
Less snow in treeline, track had very thin coverage in treeline. 
Up on the pass there was minimal coverage but on lee slopes HS 50-60cm. Most other parts about 30-35. 
Pass is “skiiable”

reports.title: 1st day of the season!
reports.text: When I got out of my car, I was worried at the only other car at the parking lot had two hikers. I strapped my skis and boots to my backpack, and headed out with my hikers. Fortunately I did not have to walk for long; I quickly shifted to skinning. The Connaught creek uptrack is 95% covered, with most of the bare patches at the beginning of the route. Initially the snow coverage was minimal (1cm a

reports.title: Early-Season Asulkan Assault
reports.text: Brought the snowshoes but managed to hike with them on my back all the way to the hut. Travel time one way was two-and-a-half hours from parking lot. Way spottier snow coming through the woods than when I did it this time last year. Ground cover gets pretty consistent past the turnoff for Great Glacier. Watch for some exposed icy sections after the turnoff for Glacier Crest and stick to the snow.

reports.title: Better than expected
reports.text:
McCrae. 
HS @ TL ~40cm, @ toe of glacier 70cm, @ top of ridge 2220m NW asp as low as 10cm. 
Widespread large surface hoar sz 2-4cm. Most predominant in open sheltered BTL and in ALP.
Dug a quick pit in N asp. open TL meadow to investigate layering, results in photo.
Skiing on the glacier was surprisingly good! Consolidated soft snow. No signs of instability observed. Entrance and exit on the summe

reports.title: Avery’s pit
reports.text: Pretty good coverage. Parked at warming hut and skinned up from there. Still sharks and thinner in the trees. Dug a “pit” at 2100m, 5cm crust 15cm down with facets underneath crust. Bottom layer consolidated. Got some pretty awesome turns in.

reports.title: Pocaterra Ridge
reports.text:
Light snow with temps between -10 to -5 with light winds.
The new summer trail had just enough snow for an easy approach and exit. 
In the trees at 2200m, HS was 30cm consisting of 5 cm of new snow over a breakable melt freeze crust with facets below. Small Surface hoar in the south alpine.
At 2400m on the South aspect of Pocaterra Ridge there was 5-10 cm of crust/ new snow. Easy to skin up but hi

reports.title: day 1
reports.text:
less than a foot of snow at 1900m.
could drive a truck to 1700m no problem

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows, Newfie Bowl
reports.text:
Weather: Sunny and calm. 
Snowpack: HS 35 cm in the meadows, from the surface down:
3–7 mm surface hoar on the surface
10 cm of low-density powder (no wind effect yet)
4 cm breakable temperature crust (1F-, soft) This layer will continue to facet out.
19 cm of low-density, sugary facets (F very soft)
Travel: Got a few good hesitant turns on grass bottom meadows. Only hit a few small rocks.
Avalanc

reports.text:
Skied the north side of Black Tusk. Ski quality was decent, bit wind affected near ridgetop. 
Consistent snow on trail started ~1300m. Switched to skinning at ~1500m. 
HS 20 cm in the meadows near the Black Tusk Junction. Coverage is honestly marginal and many slopes at tree line are likely still below threshold. Didn’t probe in the alpine but north aspects are skiable.

reports.title: White at McLatchie, but only just …
reports.text:
Out for a (hiking boots) wander around McLatchie on Wednesday 18th Nov
-3 in the morning, 0 by 4pm at 1700m, calm, overcast.
Effectively no snow below 1500m, 30cm to 40cm at our high point of 1800m. See photo for ‘profile’.
Road graded thru Harvey … no word on if that will continue.

reports.title: Shulaps Boniness
reports.text:
Hiked up Shulaps from Marshal Lake road, route is primarily on southern aspects.
Very little snow until ~2000m where there was a up to 10cm. Above that very wind scoured and thin. Isolated pockets of up to 50cm of powder but generally bony. Surface hoar and faceted snow ready to get buried.

reports.title: Lazy day at Sunshine Meadows
reports.text: Snow pack was highly variable from place to place - everything from just 5cm of new snow on bare rock, to HS 50cm with 15 to 20cm of drifted snow above a thin melt-freeze crust with sugar below. Where present, the crust was supportive. Ski pen varied from near zero to 15cm. Wind varied from none to a light breeze. Reasonably heavy overcast. Deep drifted snow lulled me briefly into forgetting about

reports.title: Metal Dome
reports.text: Went for a look with the new snow and expectations were exceeded. Road in good shape to parking with no snow. Walked ~25min to where trees change to open meadows and started skiing on ~30-50cm base at 1650m. Travel was only possible on skis where old snow existed underneath the fresh storm snow. At ~1850m on the N glacier, probed 185cm. Top 100cm was F-1F progressive density sitting on old snow/me

reports.title: Maddysparklez Megamind Mission
reports.text: Up to 30cm of well consolidated snow at 1800m with 5-10cm accumulating over 24hours. Graupel & some stellar stellars overnight. Lots of wind, not much transport at our elevation. Lower elevations lost snow coverage quickly. Paw pen 5cm tested by our dawg. 10/10 would recommend an early season mission.

reports.title: Scoping out snow at Zoa
reports.text: Hiked up to the ridge to scope out the snow and do some avi rescue practice but left the skis in the car… seemed like too much boot packing for us. There was 35cm of snow on the ridge a lot of sharks. Saw a couple folks out doing a few laps though!

reports.title: Hope you like rocks, cause we’ve got heaps of f*cking rocks
reports.text: Went for a trundle up hermit today to see how the alpine is shaping up. Snow line is sitting around 1650m. You can still basically hike up to the campground. I ditched the trail runners after 2.5km of hiking and managed to break some kind of a trail on skins from just below 1800m. Freezing level came up disgustingly high over the weekend, precip was still falling as rain at 2000m in the afternoon.

reports.title: Should have brought skates
reports.text:
6-8 inches of snow for the entire trail and even less above the lower lake.
Significant surface hoar forming throughout the day. Facets at ground level. Lower lake is frozen enough for skating but the area is not skiable yet.
